When a value depends on environment or backend selection (base URLs, feature endpoints, timeouts, CLI flags with env-var fallbacks), resolve it through one shared, well-tested function rather than letting each call site re-derive it independently. Divergent resolution logic is a recurring source of bugs: one surface used the account's resolved backend (`resolveAccountApiBaseUrl`, honoring a provider `baseUrl` override) while a sibling surface used `getClineEnvironmentConfig().appBaseUrl` directly, so a staging override with `CLINE_ENVIRONMENT` unset silently opened production. The fix was to export a single mapping helper (`resolveClineAppBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl)`) that both the CLI and the desktop sidecar call, returning `undefined` (hide the feature) for backends no known environment declares, instead of guessing.

Prefer resolving environment-derived configuration once, at the point where the environment/backend is established (e.g., process/session startup), and pass the resolved value down rather than recomputing it on every call — especially when the environment or account cannot change mid-session. For example, the desktop sidecar now resolves `clineAppBaseUrl` once during context creation and stores it on the context, instead of reading provider settings and re-resolving on every `get_cline_app_base_url` request.

When a setting can come from multiple sources (CLI flag, environment variable, default), define and document explicit precedence, and make sure every entry point that can set the flag is wired through the same resolution path. A `--no-mouse` flag was added to a test-only command builder while the real runtime path used a different inline command, so the flag silently had no effect; the fix wired the flag through the actual command, used `getOptionValueSource` to distinguish "not explicitly set" from Commander's negated-flag default, and defined precedence as subcommand flag > root flag > environment variable fallback.

Finally, when choosing environment-sensitive defaults (e.g., timeouts for cold starts), back the choice with real data (telemetry/measurements) and keep a single default shared across all clients unless there is a documented, platform-specific reason to diverge — a shared root cause (e.g., antivirus-scanned binary cold start) should get a shared fix, not divergent per-platform tuning.
